sourceIssues.locator: §5, proof of Theorem 5.2, p.386, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 187 (2018), 379–390 (publisher PDF)
sourceIssues.printed: "Define the subgroup H of ideal classes [I] in Cl(K*) such that there exists an element a ∈ K^× with t_{K,φ}(I) = (a) and Norm_{K/Q}(I) = aā for some a ∈ K^×." and later "Norm_{K/Q}(I) = r_{K,φ}(I) \overline{r_{K,φ}(I)} = aā O_K, so that aā/|O_K/I| is a totally positive unit", "aā/Norm_{K/Q}(I)".
sourceIssues.correction: I is an ideal of the reflex field K*, so read N_{K*/Q}(I) for Norm_{K/Q}(I) and |O_{K*}/I| for |O_K/I|; the ideal-level identity is t_{K,φ}(I)·\overline{t_{K,φ}(I)} = N_{K*/Q}(I)·O_K (with t, not the class-group map r).
sourceIssues.reason: The reflex norm t_{K,φ} sends ideals of K* to ideals of K, and t(I)·t(I)‾ = N_{K*/Q}(I)O_K; Norm_{K/Q} and O_K do not apply to an ideal of K*. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (item polarized-reciprocity-kernel).

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 2.2 (p.382) and the proof of Theorem 4.2 (p.385), in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 187 (2018), 379–390 (publisher PDF)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 2.2: "For a primitive CM type Φ, there are two elements in S(E, Φ) such that the lowest degree isogeny between them has degree at least |Disc(E)|^{1/4−o_g(1)}." Theorem 4.2 is stated for any A ∈ S(E, Φ), and its proof begins "Note that by Proposition 2.2, there are two elements A and B in S(E, Φ) such that the minimal isogeny between them is of degree at least |Disc(E)|^{1/4−o_g(1)}."
sourceIssues.correction: State Proposition 2.2 as: for every A ∈ S(E, Φ) there is B ∈ S(E, Φ) such that every isogeny A → B has degree at least |Disc(E)|^{1/4−o_g(1)}. This is what its proof gives, and it is what the proof of Theorem 4.2 uses for the given A.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof of Proposition 2.2 fixes an arbitrary A and counts: isogenies from A of degree n correspond to ideals of norm n, of which there are n^{o(1)}, while |S(E, Φ)| ≫ |Disc(E)|^{1/4−o(1)}. As printed, the proposition asserts only some pair, and the proof of Theorem 4.2 silently replaces the given A by that pair's first element. Noted by the extraction.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, p.382, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 187 (2018), 379–390 (publisher PDF)
sourceIssues.printed: "The Brauer–Siegel theorem [4], the fact that the regulators of E and E_0 are the same, and the fact that |Disc(E)| ≥ |Disc(E_0)|² imply that |S(E, Φ)| ≫_g |Cl(E)|/|Cl(E_0)| ≫_g |Disc(E)|^{1/4−o_g(1)}."
sourceIssues.correction: The regulators agree up to a bounded factor: R_E = (2^{g−1}/Q)·R_{E_0}, where Q = [O_E^× : μ_E O_{E_0}^×] ∈ {1, 2} is the Hasse unit index. That suffices for the estimate.
sourceIssues.reason: For a CM field of degree 2g the regulator ratio is 2^{g−1}/Q (e.g. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, Proposition 4.16), which is 1 only when g = 1, or g = 2 and Q = 2. The factor depends only on g, so the displayed bound is unchanged. Noted by the extraction.
